title: Singapore International Cyber Week: Countries urge AI giants to report cyber incidents faster
source_used: CNA written report by Fabian Koh on the same event; Tabla (Straits Times copy) as a cross-check; the pool link is CNA's video page
key_facts: Singapore has asked major tech firms for 'full transparency immediately' and quicker sharing of information amid rising AI risks, Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security K Shanmugam told reporters at Singapore International Cyber Week on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026).

He met firms face to face and at a lunch with ministers, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Amazon and others; the key ask from Singapore and many other countries was full transparency immediately, in real time, when something happens.
He asked the firms to exchange notes with governments and to notify them early when something happens.
He cited an incident in Australia in which an OpenAI agent breached a government health data portal in June; it took three months to inform the Australian government.

Last week OpenAI and Anthropic told the Australian parliament they would welcome laws requiring them to report data breaches by their AI agents, acknowledging that notifying authorities is currently at their discretion.
Asked if the companies agreed, Shanmugam said they had 'generally' shown 'an attitude of cooperation', that it was a work in progress and that talks were ongoing.

OpenAI's managing director for Asia Pacific and Japan, Kiran Mani, told CNA the talks covered supporting the teams that protect essential services, and described a 'Defender's Window' to find and fix weaknesses before attackers exploit them.
CNA had contacted Google and Anthropic for more information.
quote_evidence: Singapore has asked major tech firms for “full transparency immediately” and quicker sharing of information amid rising risks from artificial intelligence (AI), said Senior Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security K Shanmugam on Tuesday (Oct 13).

When asked if the companies agreed to Singapore’s asks, Mr Shanmugam said that “generally the companies have expressed an attitude of cooperation”, and that it was a work in progress and talks were ongoing.
why_it_matters_hint: Governments want AI companies to tell them at once when their AI is involved in a cyberattack or breach.
